newsitem.title: USA: CBOT task force urges members pass delivery change.
newsitem.headline: CBOT task force urges members pass delivery change.

text.p: The chairman of the Chicago Board of Trade Grain Delivery Task Force on Tuesday launched a last-minute effort to urge members to vote in favor of a proposal to change the corn and soybean delivery system.
"With so much controversy on this issue, it may be tempting not to vote at all," William Evans, task force chairman, wrote in a circular to CBOT members.
"Today, on this vote, not voting is choosing to let someone outside this exchange make this decision."
CBOT members vote Tuesday on the controversial proposal, which responds to government pressure to expand storage.

The proposal would put delivery locations along the Illinois River from Pekin, Ill., to Chicago. The plan also allows for delivery at Burns Harbor, Ind., but eliminates Toledo and St. Louis as delivery points.
Results of the vote should be available at 1600 CDT (2100 GMT).

The CBOT task force was established after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in December told the CBOT that the traditional delivery terms for its corn and soybean contracts were no longer suitable due to shrinking Chicago storage space and changes in cash grain marketing.
CFTC said it would make its own recommendations if the exchange failed to come up with a solution.
"If this vote fails, we fail to take responsibility to make our own decisions, and we may permanently alter who is in charge of this institution," Evans wrote.
Opposition from commercial grain firms has been mounting against the proposal in recent weeks, CBOT traders said.
A petition circulated on the trading floor last Friday was signed by about a dozen commercial firms, outlining their opposition to the proposal, they said.
Evans said in the release that the membership should not allow commercial opposition alone sway the vote.
"I know that a lot of pressure is being put on certain brokers and commission houses by commercials who have chosen to lead the fight against these recommendations," Evans said.

"Don't forget, these are the same commercials who led the opposition to the previous task force proposal to add the Northern Illinois River and Milwaukee to the existing delivery points of Chicago and Toledo.
"Now these same commercials are arguing for an alternative that would do just that," Evans said.
